panels.title: Caches — hit rate, throughput, evictions, size
Memory — working set vs GC heap
Investigate one request: paste a trace id or correlation id

options.content:
**Paste an id into the `find` variable at the top of the dashboard, then widen the time range to cover when it happened.**

| Where the id comes from | What it looks like | Which panel below answers |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Correlation-ID` response header (every response has one) | `a8faac35-f23e-…` | **Logs for one request** |
| `traceId` inside an RFC 7807 error body — `00-<trace id>-<span id>-01` | paste **only the middle part** | both panels |
| `TraceID` field on any log line in **What is failing** | 32 hex characters | **The trace** |
| `correlationId` on an audit record in Kibana | `a8faac35-f23e-…` | **Logs for one request** |

The logs panel matches either id. The trace panel needs a trace id and will error on a correlation id, which is expected rather than a broken panel.

A red error triangle on **The trace** usually means the id is not in Tempo at all: Tempo answers 404 and Grafana shows that as an error, not as "No data". Check you copied all 32 characters, and remember Tempo has its own retention — an id from yesterday may simply be gone.
